Question B-003-021-008.

Why the correct answer is right: In free space the same radiated power spreads over the surface of a sphere, so power density follows an inverse-square pattern with distance.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "It decreases as the square of the distance": This is the correct choice because in free space the same radiated power spreads over the surface of a sphere, so power density follows an inverse-square pattern with distance.
- sourceIndex 1: "It decreases linearly with the distance": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from It decreases as the square of the distance. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, reducing that quantity is not the mechanism that produces the correct effect here.
- sourceIndex 2: "It decreases in inverse proportion to the distance": This answer would fit a different fault than It decreases as the square of the distance. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, reducing that quantity is not the mechanism that produces the correct effect here.
- sourceIndex 3: "It decreases at a rate depending on ground absorption": This option confuses another station topic with It decreases as the square of the distance. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, reducing that quantity is not the mechanism that produces the correct effect here.
